measured.heard: Main calls factorial of 3, and factorial calls itself with n minus 1, until n is 1. Each call to factorial gets its own n and its own r. This lesson draws each call to factorial as a frame on the call stack. Now factorial of 3 cannot finish line 7 until factorial of 2 returns a value, so its frame waits under the new one. In this lesson's drawing, the empty box after r equals 3 times stands for the value factorial of 2 has not returned yet. Then factorial of 2 calls factorial of 1, so 3 factorial frames now sit on top of main. The next scene answers this question. In factorial of 1, n greater than 1 is false, so r stays 1 and it returns 1. Each factorial return hands its value to the call that made it 1 frame down. Factorial of 2 gets 1 and returns 2 times 1 equals 2. Then factorial of 3 gets 2 and returns 3 times 2 equals 6 to main. Main stores the 6 in its own r and prints main got 6. The calls start in the order 3, 2, 1, and they finish in the reverse order. 1, 2, 3. In this lesson's drawing, the stack grows by 1 frame for each factorial call and shrinks by 1 for each factorial return. Each factorial return value flows to the frame below.
